messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas (as of 2024)** | Topic | Key Points | Notes | |-------|------------|-------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits vary by road type:
• 55 mph on rural interstates,
• 65 mph on urban interstates,
• 45 mph on rural highways,
• 35 mph on urban highways,
• 25 mph in school zones (unless posted otherwise). | Speed limits are enforced by both police and automated speed cameras. | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All drivers and front‑seat passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• Children under 5 must be in a rear‑seat child‑safety seat. | Failure to comply can result in a $50 fine and points on the driver’s record. | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Violations carry a $50 fine and 1 point. | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• For commercial drivers, the limit is 0.04 %.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas has a “zero‑tolerance” law for drivers under 21 (BAC ≥ 0.02 %). | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • At uncontrolled intersections, the driver on the right has the right of way.
• Pedestrians have priority at crosswalks. | Failure to yield can lead to a $50 fine and points. | | **School Bus** | • Drivers must stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and lights flashing.
• Must remain stopped until the bus resumes motion or the stop sign is retracted. | Violations can result in a $200 fine and points. | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during any weather that reduces visibility.
• Fog lights may be used in fog, but only if headlights are also on. | Failure to use headlights when required can lead to a $50 fine. | | **Towing & Vehicle Registration** | • Vehicles must display a valid registration sticker.
• Towing a vehicle requires a valid towing permit. | Unregistered vehicles can be towed and fined. | | **Parking** | • No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces (unless you have a permit), or on sidewalks.
• Parking in a “no parking” zone is a $50 fine. | Violations can also result in vehicle impoundment. | | **Traffic Signals & Signs** | • Red light = stop; green light = go; yellow light = prepare to stop.
• Stop signs require a full stop. | Running a red light or stop sign can lead to a $200 fine and points. | | **Points System** | • Texas uses a points system for traffic violations.
• Accumulating 12 points in 3 years can lead to license suspension. | Points are removed after 3 years of no violations. | | **Insurance** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for total bodily injury, $25,000 for property damage. | Driving without insurance can result in license suspension and fines. | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles must wear helmets.
• Commercial vehicles must follow specific weight and safety regulations. | Helmet use is mandatory for riders under 18. | | **Roadside Assistance & Emergency** | • In emergencies, use the 911 line.
• Roadside assistance is available through the Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT). | TxDOT provides free roadside assistance for registered vehicles. | ### Quick Reference - **Speed Limits**: 55–65 mph on interstates, 45–35 mph on highways, 25 mph in school zones. - **Seat‑Belt**: Mandatory for all occupants. - **Cell‑Phone**: Hand‑held prohibited. - **DUI**: BAC ≥ 0.08 % (0.04 % for commercial). - **Right‑of‑Way**: Right side has priority at uncontrolled intersections. - **School Bus**: Stop until lights retract. - **Headlights**: On from sunset to sunrise or in low visibility. - **Parking**: No parking in fire lanes, handicap spaces, or sidewalks. For the most up‑to‑date and detailed information, consult the Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) website or the Texas Transportation Code.
